issues.legal_issue: A law that imposes a collection disability on one group but not on comparable groups violates the guarantee of equal protection when no reasonable basis for the distinction is established.
material_facts: A law required the government to collect revenue previously collected by jagirdars and, after deducting expenses, pay it to the jagirdars; an amendment extended the provision to taxes, cesses and forest revenue.
After territorial integration, jagirdars in the area governed by the provision faced this collection disability, while jagirdars in other areas of the same State did not.
The State did not allege or substantiate that the affected jagirdars or their tenures had any substantial distinguishing feature that justified the different treatment.
The challenged provisions remained in force when the Constitution commenced, and the affected holder sought relief against their operation.
issues.conclusion: The provision as amended was void because it contravened the guarantee of equality and equal protection; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 13(1) and 14 of the Constitution, a law in force that is inconsistent with the guarantee of equality is void to the extent of the inconsistency. A classification must bear a reasonable and just relation to the subject of the law, and unequal treatment requires a substantial distinction supporting it. The Court distinguished Frank J. Bowman v. Edward A. Lewis (101 U.S. 22; 25 Law. Ed. 989), where territorial arrangements could be justified by municipal considerations; Ramjilal v. Income Tax Officer, Mohindargarh ([1951] S.C.R. 127), which concerned a reasonable classification for concluding pending proceedings under the law applicable when rights or liabilities accrued; and The State of Punjab v. Ajaib Singh ([1953] S.C.R. 254), where a geographical classification was justified by the similar interests of the class concerned. The Court also noted that Thakur Madan Singh v. Collector of Sikar (Rajasthan Law Weekly, 1954, p. 1) involved a supported basis for classification and distinguished the challenged provision here.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_law and unequal_collection_disability_imposed_on_one_group and comparable_groups_left_unburdened and no_substantial_distinction_shown

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law: A person challenged the validity of a law on the ground that it denied equal protection.
predicates.unequal_collection_disability_imposed_on: The law required one group to surrender or lose control over collection of revenue that it had previously collected.
predicates.comparable_groups_left_unburdened: The law left comparable groups outside the affected group free from the same collection disability.
predicates.no_substantial_distinction_shown: The government did not establish a substantial difference between the affected group and the unburdened groups that justified their different treatment.

issues.definition: When a law challenged for denying equal protection burdens one group with a collection disability, leaves comparable groups unburdened, and no substantial distinction is shown, the challenged law is void for unequal protection.
